candidates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE)
support_spans: A 22-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
candidates.why: The patient's history of SLE and presentation of erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution are consistent with ACLE.

candidates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)
support_spans: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
candidates.why: The presence of atypical target lesions and blisters across the body are consistent with SJS.

candidates.name: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN)
support_spans: Flaccid bullae and target lesions
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
candidates.why: The presence of flaccid bullae, target lesions, and full thickness epithelial necrosis on biopsy are consistent with TEN.
